stories.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
stories.reason: Anthropic's flagship Fable/Mythos 5.2 release with major benchmark gains (FrontierSWE v2 69.9% vs 62.3%, Humanity's Last Exam 74.2% vs 67.7%) and a dedicated cyber-verification model; official primary source.
key_facts: Fable 5.2 API id claude-fable-5-2; Mythos 5.2 gated via Cyber/Life Sciences Verification Programs
Pricing $8/$40 per Mtok input/output, fast mode $16/$80
FrontierSWE v2 69.9% vs Opus 5.5's 62.3%; Humanity's Last Exam 74.2% vs 67.7%
Mythos 5.2 finds 10.2% more CVEs than Opus 5.5, 14.4% more than Mythos 5.1
Formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours using ~1,000 agents
Sandbox escape rate 3.1%, close to Opus 5.5's 3.3%; automated behavioral audit score 2.67 vs Opus 5.5's 2.79

stories.title: Taiwan-Based Hacker Used BOSSAI AI Agents to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records
stories.reason: Documented real-world campaign: a single Taiwan-based attacker ran 12 AI agents (BOSSAI) against hundreds of orgs in 11+ countries, breaching ~10 including Taipei's emergency dispatch system; concrete AI-offense case study with primary research (Acronis) behind it.
key_facts: 12 AI agents built (9 active); Grok/MiniMax M3 refused direct attack requests, abliterated DeepSeek/GLM/Qwen models did the attacking
Pulled Taipei 119 dispatch records for 7 districts via API; exposed 2018 patient ECG/ambulance video with no login
~206,800 Mexican phone records taken; SQL injection against Thai universities
Agents hallucinated CVEs; over half of one scanner's high/critical findings were false positives
Attacker deanonymized via reused GitHub/SSH-key identity and a home IP leaked in a Grok chat log

stories.title: Backporting security fixes at scale with Codex
stories.reason: Trail of Bits built a working Codex-based pipeline that has already landed fixes for 149 CVEs into stable Linux kernels plus Fedora/Ubuntu packages — running code with hard numbers, exactly the kind of AI x cyber result the profile wants.
key_facts: 149 distinct CVEs backported into stable Linux kernel releases as of Oct 29
Simple backport ~30 min human attention, complex one ~3 hours, down from days
5.10.y alone had 2,006 unfixed kernel CVEs as of Sept 18; Debian 13 had 4,562 unique unfixed CVEs
Public tracker: trailofbits.github.io/ptp-linux-stable-cve-dashboard

stories.title: Alleged AI-aided cyberattack exploits assistant interface to breach German web host
stories.reason: A real breach through a flaw in a customer-facing MCP server (Mittwald), compromising 56 customer projects — a concrete agent/MCP attack chain, the exact category the taste profile flags as always-surface.
key_facts: Flaw in Mittwald's MCP server used to connect AI assistants to its mStudio hosting platform
56 customer projects compromised; attacker undetected for 8 days
First probed in October during the PHP2Shell patch scramble
Director says logs suggest AI-paced actions (steps completed in seconds) but offered no other evidence

stories.title: Ginux: A New Kernel Runs Linux Userspace, Made via Human-Directed AI Engineering
stories.reason: A single persistent coding-agent task built a Rust x86-64 kernel from scratch in 11 days that boots a real Rocky Linux 10 userspace under systemd — a concrete, reproducible (repo linked) demonstration of agentic systems engineering, not a vendor claim.
key_facts: Author Gregory Kurtzer (CIQ); published as 'Ginux' on Zenodo Oct 27
Boots via UEFI, implements a Linux compatibility layer, runs unmodified Alpine binaries
Boots Rocky Linux 10 userspace through multi-user.target
Repo: github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux; no independent security audit; status flagged 'Concept'

stories.title: RunanywhereAI/trnrt
stories.reason: TrnRT is a real, actively maintained (315 commits, 385 stars) open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium2 with fused decode kernels and a device/host prefix cache — a concrete serving-infra project, which the profile weighs over training work.
key_facts: OpenAI-compatible API from a single trn2.48xlarge instance
Runs GLM-5.3-Flash (320B MoE, 1M context) via fused NKI decode kernels
385 stars, 6 forks, CI + security-scorecard badges
Self-reported benchmark: outputs matched an earlier build on 384/384 requests

stories.title: Muse Ember: Our smallest, most efficient model
stories.reason: Meta's new smallest/most efficient model (Muse Ember) beats Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna on several agent benchmarks at roughly a third of the cost — a legitimate efficiency-tier release with head-to-head numbers against current frontier small models.
key_facts: Model id muse-ember-1.0; 1M-token context, up to 512K output
AutomationBench-AA 37.8% vs Luna 20.2%/Haiku 13.9%; matches Haiku's best score at ~1/3 the cost
Pricing $0.10/$0.50 per Mtok (<=200K prompt), $0.30/$1.50 beyond
Parameter count not disclosed; open-weight status not stated

stories.title: Asahi Linux Drops MIT, Goes Full GPL After AI Used to Steal Unreleased Code
stories.reason: Asahi Linux is relicensing all repos from MIT to GPLv2+ specifically because actors were running its code through LLMs to launder its origin and commercialize it — a concrete governance response to AI-enabled IP laundering, not just a policy opinion.
key_facts: Asahi cites code 'rewritten with AI to obscure its source' and republished without credit
Project already bans AI-generated contributions
Compared to WINE's 2002 MIT-to-LGPL move to block proprietary forks
OpenBSD dev criticized relicensing without all prior contributors' consent
